nodes.title: קטע G
nodes.body_he: הכותב לא אומר שהסדנה היא צדקה. הוא אומר שהיא נשארת כשיש חובה ותשלום קטן.
nodes.body_content: Cities tell young people to learn a trade and then act surprised when those people leave. A trade needs tools, a first client, and a room that does not cost more than the wage. In many towns the room is the part that fails. A carpenter can borrow tools. He cannot borrow a rent that doubles in a year. Some councils answer with a shared workshop: one address, many benches, a lease the city holds. The idea is not charity. The city keeps a worker who would otherwise take the skill to another place. Critics say a shared bench teaches people to wait for help. The record in the towns that tried it is plainer. The workshops that lasted charged a small fee, kept a waiting list, and asked every member to teach one hour a month. The workshops that were free and had no duty closed within a year. A skill grows when the room stays, and the room stays when someone besides the learner pays attention.
